title: Fully Secure Constant-Call Tweakable Blockciphers in the Standard PRP Model
summary: Thirty-two constructions achieve full provable security with minimal blockcipher calls in the ideal-blockcipher model; constant-call full security in the standard PRP model remains open.

formal_statement.body: Thirty-two tweakable-blockcipher constructions achieve full provable security with a minimum number of blockcipher calls in the ideal-blockcipher model. Determine whether fully secure tweakable blockciphers can instead be constructed in the standard pseudorandom-permutation model using only a constant number of blockcipher calls.

scope.domain: Provably secure tweakable-blockcipher design from classical blockciphers.
assumptions: The underlying blockcipher satisfies the standard pseudorandom-permutation assumption.
parameters: Blockcipher-call count: the construction must use only a constant number of calls
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a fully secure tweakable blockcipher can be constructed in the standard pseudorandom-permutation model with a constant number of blockcipher calls.

citations.label: How to Build Fully Secure Tweakable Blockciphers from Classical Blockciphers

progress.summary: The conclusion presents this as future work after reporting 32 fully secure constructions with a minimum number of blockcipher calls in the ideal-blockcipher model. It leaves the constant-call construction in the standard PRP model unresolved.
citation_labels: Lei Wang et al., How to Build Fully Secure Tweakable Blockciphers from Classical Blockciphers
